statement: Or-opt1 (single-city relocation with KNN candidates) adds ~0.06 points to 2-opt + ILS for penalized TSP problem #44, yielding 78.97 vs 78.91. Or-opt2 (pair relocation) and or-opt3 (triple relocation) cause TLE on large N even with efficient memmove implementations. Only or-opt1 is safe within the 2s time budget.
regime: N up to 200K, 2s time limit, K=15 KNN, G=sqrt(N/2.5) grid
mechanism: Or-opt1 explores the relocation neighborhood (remove city, reinsert elsewhere) which is disjoint from 2-opt's reversal neighborhood. After 2-opt convergence, ~5% of cities have positive removal gain and some of those have improving insertion points near KNN neighbors. The improvement is small because 2-opt already captures most local improvements.
applicability_bounds: Applies to TSP-like problems with 2s time limit and N up to 200K. The ~0.06 point improvement is at the edge of measurement noise for single judge runs; confidence is medium. For problems with more generous time limits, or-opt2/3 might also be viable.

statement: dist² early rejection before eucl() in candidate-list 2-opt provides a minor speedup by avoiding sqrt for most non-improving candidates. This may contribute to TLE avoidance: v32 (with dist² rejection) showed 0 TLE in 5+ runs vs v25 (without) showing 2 TLE in 6 runs, though the evidence is circumstantial.
mechanism: dist²(a,c) = (xa-xc)²+(ya-yc)² is computed with 2 subtractions, 2 multiplications, and 1 addition (~5 cycles). eucl() adds sqrt (~20 cycles). For K=15 candidates per city where ~80% are rejected by dist², the savings are ~270 cycles/city × N cities per pass. For N=200K, this saves ~18ms per pass.
applicability_bounds: The TLE-avoidance effect is circumstantial (small sample). The dist² check is always safe to add and never hurts performance.
